thesis: Round 1's mechanism was post-shock drift: a true-range day well above its own ATR(14) that closes in the direction of the move is the market printing new information faster than participants can absorb it, and slow-moving capital re-rates the name over days rather than instantly. Round 2 asks whether that mechanism, and the comparable-volatility-cohort fix for the engine's single fixed stop_loss_pct/position_pct, survive leaving the sector I was forced into. I measured ATR(14)/close (trailing-252-session mean, same method as my round-1 card) across all 93 round-2 symbols through 2026-02-13: it spans 0.119% (SHY) to 4.137% (ARKG), roughly 35x -- and one name, SLV, is worth flagging on its own: its trailing mean is a moderate 2.908%, but its most recent single-day ATR/close is 13.2% because the design window ends inside what the bars show as a real short squeeze (SLV round-tripped roughly $67->$110->$69 in three weeks). That is event-driven, not persistent, vol -- exactly the kind a fixed stop should not be sized around. One correction to the round-2 brief's framing: measured this way, the round-2 spread (35x, or ~120x if SLV's last-day reading is used instead of its trailing mean) is actually narrower than round 1's 43-symbol spread (SGOV 0.035% to OKLO 10.513%, ~300x, matching the ~260x my round-1 card reported from rounded figures) -- so 'wider still' does not hold under my round-1 methodology applied consistently, though the underlying point (one stop cannot span either roster) is unaffected by which multiple it is. What round 2 actually adds is choice of cohort, not a bigger spread: I built a 6-symbol comparable-vol band -- TLT (0.979%), DBC (1.190%), EWJ (1.300%), XLU (1.465%), XLP (1.191%), INDA (0.969%) -- max/min ratio 1.51x, tighter than round 1's 1.6x, and this time drawn from four different macro drivers (long-duration US rates, a diversified commodity basket, Japanese and Indian equities, US utilities, US staples) instead of one semiconductor/momentum-tech sector. Pairwise daily-return correlation among these six (trailing 252 sessions): mean 21.7%, median 22.7%, max 50.4% (XLU-XLP), min -12.6% (TLT-DBC, genuinely negative) -- against my round-1 cohort's mean 48.8%, median 49.9%, max 72.1%, min 22.0%, all-positive. Comparable volatility without correlated exposure, which round 1's universe could not offer, is real and roughly halves both the average and the worst-case pairwise correlation while tightening the vol band slightly further. ATR/price persistence (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.98-0.99, lag-5 0.72-0.88 across the six) confirms these are multi-week vol regimes, not one-day noise, so an ATR-relative trigger is still measuring something real here. The one thing that did not transfer: round 1's exact entry (range > 1.5x ATR, close > open, close > sma(50)) fires 0-10 times per name per year on this cohort -- TLT and EWJ fired zero times in 252 sessions -- because index/bond ETFs absorb macro news continuously through arbitrage and duration-matched flow rather than producing the discrete, story-driven surprise days a single momentum stock does, and because sma(50) is a multi-month trend filter that fights a rates/carry-driven instrument's naturally choppier path. I dropped the sma(50) filter (it was measuring long-run direction, not the shock-absorption speed this discipline is about) and lowered the multiplier to 1.2x ATR, which restores 7-29 signals per name per year (85/year total across the six) while keeping the core condition: today's range must exceed its own recent typical range, and the session must close in the direction of the expansion. Stop and target are scaled from round 1's numbers by the ratio of mean ATR/price between the two cohorts (1.182% here vs 4.76% in round 1, a 0.25x factor): 10%->2.5% stop, 15%->3.75%(rounded to 4%) target, preserving the same ATR-multiple risk/reward geometry (RRR 1.5-1.6) rather than picking new round numbers. The counterparty on the other side of the trade is whoever is still transacting at the pre-shock price or NAV while the flow catches up: authorized participants and market makers absorbing creation/redemption lag, index rebalancers still executing against stale weights, or foreign-flow investors reacting to the same macro print a day late.
entry: high - low > atr(14) * 1.2 and close > open
